question: You are turning into a side road and a pedestrian is waiting to cross it. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn them
Give way and let them cross
Speed up to clear the turn
Wave them to stay on the kerb
explain: Rule H2: You should give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting. To cross a road into which or from which you are turning.

question: Does Rule H2 apply when you turn out of a. Side road as well as when you turn into one?
options: Yes, both turning into and out of a road
explain: Rule H2 covers pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross. A road you are turning into or out of.

question: Before stopping to let a pedestrian cross a side road you are turning into. What should you check?
options: Your mirrors so you brake safely
explain: Rule H2: Check your mirrors early. So you can slow down smoothly without surprising traffic behind.

question: If a pedestrian has already stepped into the road you are turning into. What must you do?
explain: Rule 170: You must give way to pedestrians. Already crossing the road you are turning into.

question: Why should you not wave a pedestrian across when stopping at a junction?
options: Another vehicle may not see them or may overtake
explain: Rule H2: Wait patiently without waving so the pedestrian checks for other traffic themselves.

question: A person with a white cane is waiting. At a side road you plan to turn into. What should you do?
options: Stop in good time and give way
explain: Rule H2: Give extra care. Patience to pedestrians who may need more time to cross.

question: Who has priority at the top of the Highway Code hierarchy of road users?
explain: Rule H1: Pedestrians are at greatest risk. Sit at the top of the road-user hierarchy.

question: When turning left into a side road, where should you look for waiting pedestrians?
options: Along the pavement and crossing point of the side road
explain: Rule H2: Scan the side road pavement early before you start steering into the turn.
